3:1.sourceText: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν πάλιν εἰς συναγωγήν, καὶ ἦν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπος ἐξηραμμένην ἔχων τὴν χεῖρα·
3:1.targetText: And He entered again into the synagogue, and there was there a man having the hand withered,

3:2.sourceText: καὶ παρετήρουν αὐτὸν εἰ τοῖς σάββασιν θεραπεύσει αὐτόν, ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ.
3:2.targetText: and they were watching Him, whether on the Sabbaths He will heal him, that they might accuse Him.

groups.note: The dative article with Sabbaths supplies the temporal on the relation in English.

3:3.sourceText: καὶ λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ τὴν χεῖρα ἔχοντι ξηράν Ἔγειρε εἰς τὸ μέσον.
3:3.targetText: And He says to the man having the hand withered, “Rise up in the midst.”

groups.note: Greek εἰς marks movement into the midst; LSV renders the resulting central position in the midst.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

3:4.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν ἀγαθὸν ποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀποκτεῖναι; οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων.
3:4.targetText: And He says to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbaths to do good, or to do evil? To save life, or to kill?” But they were silent.

groups.note: The dative article with Sabbaths supplies the temporal on the relation in English.

3:5.sourceText: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος αὐτοὺς μετ’ ὀργῆς, συνλυπούμενος ἐπὶ τῇ πωρώσει τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν, λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρα. καὶ ἐξέτεινεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ.
3:5.targetText: And having looked around on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their heart, He says to the man, “Stretch forth your hand”; and he stretched forth, and his hand was restored whole as the other;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV supplies the possessive in your hand; N1904 has the hand without a possessive pronoun.
LSV has an additional restoration comparison whole as the other; these words are absent from the pinned N1904 verse.

3:6.sourceText: καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εὐθὺς μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν συμβούλιον ἐδίδουν κατ’ αὐτοῦ, ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν.
3:6.targetText: and the Pharisees having gone forth, immediately, with the Herodians, were taking counsel against Him how they might destroy Him.

groups.note: Greek giving counsel is a deliberation idiom, rendered were taking counsel; the whole counsel-plus-verb predicate is kept together.

3:7.sourceText: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἀνεχώρησεν πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ πολὺ πλῆθος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἠκολούθησεν· καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας
3:7.targetText: And Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed Him, and from Judea,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV makes the followed person explicit as Him; N1904 has no object pronoun with followed here.

3:8.sourceText: καὶ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰδουμαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου καὶ περὶ Τύρον καὶ Σιδῶνα, πλῆθος πολύ, ἀκούοντες ὅσα ποιεῖ, ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.
3:8.targetText: and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea and beyond the Jordan; and they around Tyre and Sidon—a great multitude—having heard how He was doing great things, came to Him.

groups.note: N1904 uses the present hearing participle; LSV uses having heard for the same hearing event.

Greek ὅσα, how many things/as much as, gives the extent of what He does; LSV renders this as how He was doing great things. The whole quantifying/content expression is linked, not a claim that ὅσα alone means an adjective great.
Greek present He does is rendered with an English past progressive He was doing.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV supplies a participant pronoun with around Tyre and Sidon; the Greek prepositional expression has no explicit they pronoun.

3:9.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα πλοιάριον προσκαρτερῇ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον, ἵνα μὴ θλίβωσιν αὐτόν·
3:9.targetText: And He said to His disciples that a little boat may wait on Him, because of the multitude, that they may not press on Him,

groups.note: Actual dative article and disciples noun jointly supply to ... disciples as the saying recipients. The intervening His retains its separate actual personal-pronoun anchor.

3:10.sourceText: πολλοὺς γὰρ ἐθεράπευσεν, ὥστε ἐπιπίπτειν αὐτῷ ἵνα αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται ὅσοι εἶχον μάστιγας.
3:10.targetText: for He healed many, so that they threw themselves on Him, in order to touch Him—as many as had plagues;

groups.note: The Greek falling/rushing-upon infinitive is rendered reflexively as they threw themselves on; this is the whole motion predicate, not a separate Greek themselves pronoun.

3:11.sourceText: καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα, ὅταν αὐτὸν ἐθεώρουν, προσέπιπτον αὐτῷ καὶ ἔκραζον λέγοντα ὅτι Σὺ εἶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ.
3:11.targetText: and the unclean spirits, when they were seeing Him, were falling down before Him, and were crying, saying, “You are the Son of God”;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
Greek ὅτι marks the direct quotation; LSV uses quotation punctuation without a separate that.

3:12.sourceText: καὶ πολλὰ ἐπετίμα αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ αὐτὸν φανερὸν ποιήσωσιν.
3:12.targetText: and many times He was charging them that they might not make Him apparent.

groups.note: The adverbial πολλά can intensify the charging, much/earnestly; LSV interprets it as repeated charging, many times. This rendering is recorded without inventing a Greek times noun.

3:13.sourceText: Καὶ ἀναβαίνει εἰς τὸ ὄρος, καὶ προσκαλεῖται οὓς ἤθελεν αὐτός, καὶ ἀπῆλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.
3:13.targetText: And He goes up to the mountain, and calls near whom He willed, and they went away to Him;

3:14.sourceText: καὶ ἐποίησεν δώδεκα ἵνα ὦσιν μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἵνα ἀποστέλλῃ αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν
3:14.targetText: and He appointed twelve, that they may be with Him, and that He may send them forth to preach,

3:15.sourceText: καὶ ἔχειν ἐξουσίαν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια·
3:15.targetText: and to have power to heal the sicknesses, and to cast out the demons.

unmappedTarget.reason: The LSV healing clause and ensuing conjunction are absent in this pinned N1904 verse, which has power to cast out demons only.

3:16.sourceText: καὶ ἐποίησεν τοὺς δώδεκα, καὶ ἐπέθηκεν ὄνομα τῷ Σίμωνι Πέτρον·
3:16.targetText: And He put on Simon the name Peter;

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 repeats and He appointed the twelve before naming Simon; LSV omits this repeated appointment clause.
Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

3:17.sourceText: καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάνην τὸν ἀδελφὸν τοῦ Ἰακώβου, καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτοῖς ὄνομα Βοανηργές, ὅ ἐστιν Υἱοὶ Βροντῆς·
3:17.targetText: and James of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, and He put on them names—Boanerges, that is, “Sons of thunder”;

groups.note: N1904 has singular name, LSV plural names; the naming noun is shared with this number difference explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article in the of-Zebedee patronymic has no separate English word.

3:18.sourceText: καὶ Ἀνδρέαν καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖον καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν Καναναῖον
3:18.targetText: and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James of Alpheus, and Thaddeus, and Simon the Zealot,

groups.note: The Greek epithet Καναναῖον transliterates the Semitic zealot designation; LSV renders its sense Zealot rather than interpreting it as a geographic Canaanite label.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article in the of-Alpheus patronymic has no separate English word.

3:19.sourceText: καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριώθ, ὃς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτόν.
3:19.targetText: and Judas Iscariot, who also delivered Him up; and they come into a house.

groups.note: The source motion verb in raw Greek 3:20 is singular He comes, while LSV at 3:19 has plural they come. The common coming predicate is linked while the additional English plural subject is separately noted.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV has the plural participant they in the house-coming clause at 3:19; the actual raw Greek clause at 3:20 has singular implicit He in ἔρχεται.

review.note: The closing house-coming clause is rendered one verse earlier in LSV than in raw N1904. Its four source words remain anchored to Greek 3:20, not to invented Greek words in 3:19.

3:20.sourceText: Καὶ ἔρχεται εἰς οἶκον· καὶ συνέρχεται πάλιν ὁ ὄχλος, ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι αὐτοὺς μηδὲ ἄρτον φαγεῖν.
3:20.targetText: And a multitude comes together again, so that they are not even able to eat bread;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

sourceMoved.reason: The initial and comes into a house clause is rendered at the end of LSV 3:19; its actual foreign-reference groups are supplied there.

3:21.sourceText: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐξῆλθον κρατῆσαι αὐτόν· ἔλεγον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξέστη.
3:21.targetText: and those alongside Him having heard, went forth to lay hold on Him, for they said that He was beside Himself,

groups.note: Greek παρά in those from/by Him identifies His own people; LSV renders the relation alongside Him. This contextual relation is retained without treating the expression as an unambiguous physical location.

3:22.sourceText: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς οἱ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καταβάντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Βεελζεβοὺλ ἔχει, καὶ ὅτι ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια.
3:22.targetText: and the scribes who [are] from Jerusalem having come down, said, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “By the ruler of the demons He casts out the demons.”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek ὅτι introduces each direct quotation, marked by English quotation punctuation without a separately translated that.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplies the relative who are from Jerusalem; no finite are verb occurs in Greek.

3:23.sourceText: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Πῶς δύναται Σατανᾶς Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλειν;
3:23.targetText: And having called them near, He said to them in allegories, “How is Satan able to cast out Satan?

3:24.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν βασιλεία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ, οὐ δύναται σταθῆναι ἡ βασιλεία ἐκείνη·
3:24.targetText: And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot be made to stand;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

3:25.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν οἰκία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ, οὐ δυνήσεται ἡ οἰκία ἐκείνη στῆναι.
3:25.targetText: and if a house is divided against itself, that house cannot be made to stand;

groups.note: N1904 has future will not be able; LSV has cannot for the same inability predicate.
Greek στῆναι is an active intransitive stand infinitive; LSV phrases it as be made to stand. The standing outcome is shared without claiming a Greek passive or extra make verb.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

3:26.sourceText: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἀνέστη ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἐμερίσθη, οὐ δύναται στῆναι ἀλλὰ τέλος ἔχει.
3:26.targetText: and if Satan rose against himself, and has been divided, he cannot be made to stand, but has an end.

groups.note: Greek active stand is expressed as English be made to stand; there is no separate source make verb or passive form.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

3:27.sourceText: ἀλλ’ οὐ δύναται οὐδεὶς εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ εἰσελθὼν τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ διαρπάσαι, ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον τὸν ἰσχυρὸν δήσῃ, καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ διαρπάσει.
3:27.targetText: No one is able to spoil the vessels of the strong man, having entered into his house, if first he may not bind the strong man, and then he will spoil his house.

groups.note: In N1904 the strong-man genitive qualifies house and his qualifies vessels; LSV instead explicitly qualifies vessels of the strong man and uses his with house. Both belongings retain the same owner, with this possessive attachment exchange recorded.
The Greek possessive modifies vessels; LSV places the same owners his with house. This same-owner possessive rearrangement is explicit, rather than an invented extra pronoun.

3:28.sourceText: Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πάντα ἀφεθήσεται τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, τὰ ἁμαρτήματα καὶ αἱ βλασφημίαι, ὅσα ἐὰν βλασφημήσωσιν·
3:28.targetText: Truly I say to you that all sins will be forgiven to the sons of men, and slanders with which they might have slandered,

groups.note: Greek ὅσα, whatever/however many, qualifies the slanders one commits; LSV renders the relative relation with which. The whole relative-content relation is linked with this grammatical recasting explicit.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

3:29.sourceText: ὃς δ’ ἂν βλασφημήσῃ εἰς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον, οὐκ ἔχει ἄφεσιν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἀλλὰ ἔνοχός ἐστιν αἰωνίου ἁμαρτήματος.
3:29.targetText: but whoever may slander in regard to the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness—throughout the age, but is in danger of continuous judgment;

groups.note: The adjective ἔνοχος denotes being liable/guilty; LSV expresses the liability as in danger. This is the whole liability predicate, not a Greek danger noun.
Greek αἰωνίου qualifies the following noun with enduring/eternal duration; LSV uses of continuous with its different judgment noun. The adjective is shared without equating the unlike nouns.

Source-witness noun difference: N1904 has ἁμαρτήματος, sin, while LSV has judgment. These unlike nouns are left unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV judgment has a different source-witness noun from pinned N1904 sin; no false sin-to-judgment lexical link is supplied.

3:30.targetText: because they said, He has an unclean spirit.”

3:31.sourceText: Καὶ ἔρχονται ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔξω στήκοντες ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς αὐτὸν καλοῦντες αὐτόν.

N1904 repeats His with mother and brothers; LSV uses one shared His for the coordinated brothers and mother, so both genuine source possessives share that English possessive.

3:35.sourceText: ὃς ἂν ποιήσῃ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ, οὗτος ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἀδελφὴ καὶ μήτηρ ἐστίν.
